newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares shuffle sideways after U.S. rally.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares shuffle sideways after U.S. rally.

text.p: Singapore shares shuffled sideways on Tuesday after a stronger overnight close on Wall Street stemmed selling pressure from foreign investors.
But dealers said the short-term direction of the market could still be downwards as there was little evidence of serious fund buying or local bargain-hunting despite recent price falls.

By the lunchtime break at 0430 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STI) was up 1.66 at 2,036.30 points, just above a 23-month low of 2,031,07 reached on Monday. Volume was a low 72.9 million shares with 112 gains and 180 falls.
"There was a small rebound this morning," said one broker.
"But, in my view, it is quite difficult for the market to go up. As a broker, I am finding it difficult recommending anyone buy today as I am afraid they may blame me tomorrow."
Of the 30 STI component stocks, car retailer Cycle & Carriage and local newspaper monopoly Singapore Press were both up 20 cents at Singapore $15.00 and S$12.30 respectively.
Multi-media firm Creative was the biggest gainer, rising S$1.10 to S$17.80 on rumours of a broker's recommendation.
Neptune Orient lines, which resumed trading on Tuesday after announcing a takeover bid for U.S.-based APL, was up eight cents at S$1.28. -- Chris Johnson, Singapore newsroom (65 8703083)
